title: Nearly Half of Kidney Transplant Candidates Never Get Started
hook: A massive national study found that nearly half of Americans referred for a kidney transplant never even begin the evaluation — and where you live can matter as much as your health.
key_points: Nearly half of Americans with kidney failure who are referred for a transplant never begin the evaluation process.
Only about 19% of those referred make it onto the transplant waitlist.
Where a person lives, marital status, income, language, age, and even the transplant center used all affect their chances.
The findings point to systemic access barriers, not just differences in medical need.
content_html: Getting referred for a kidney transplant sounds like the hard part is behind you. A massive national study covered by ScienceDaily found otherwise: nearly half of Americans with kidney failure who are referred for a transplant never even begin the evaluation process, and only about 19% make it onto the waitlist at all.
extra_html: What stands out is what predicts falling through the cracks. Researchers found that factors like where a person lives, whether they're married, their income, language, age, and even which transplant center they're referred to can dramatically change their odds of moving forward — differences that point to systemic access barriers rather than differences in medical need. For patients and families navigating kidney failure, the practical takeaway is that persistence and advocacy at each step of the referral process can matter as much as the medicine itself.

related.title: The Silent Spread of Kidney Disease
related.hook: A global study estimates chronic kidney disease now affects nearly 800 million people — often silently — making it a leading and frequently overlooked cause of death.
